source.title: Cramming: Training a Language Model on a Single GPU in One Day

record.tranche_reason: The study measures masked-language-model loss across token progress and transformer architecture variants, and reports how loss changes with model size and architecture. It does not reproduce the original scaling-law fitting procedure.
record.gate_note: Figure 1 reports MLM loss against tokens ingested for multiple transformer variants; the text describes the early and later loss trajectories. Tables 8 and 9 separately report MLM loss for architecture variants. GLUE scores and other downstream metrics are not rows for V6 because the study does not test whether downstream performance is predictable from scale or pretraining loss. Statements about other studies' scaling-law results are citations, not results from this study.
record.test_reason: In a new setting (one-day, single-GPU BERT-style MLM pretraining), the study's own MLM-loss results across many transformer shapes and details bear on V4: same-size models of different type show near-identical per-token loss behaviour. The study fits no power law, so V1 to V3 are not tested quantitatively.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors say performance in this low-compute MLM regime qualitatively follows Kaplan-style scaling laws: gains from larger models are cancelled by their slower throughput, and reshaping at similar size gives little. Gains come instead from changes that speed up gradient steps at near-constant size, and from training and data choices. No power law is fitted.
record.recipe_differences: This is a one-day, single-GPU masked-language-model study of architecture and training modifications, not a direct reproduction of the original scaling-law experiments or fitting procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report that model size affects the multiplicative shift in later loss trajectories; trajectories vary unpredictably during the first 1B tokens. Their architecture tables use distinct preliminary and final setups.

fits_no_version.finding: At a fixed one-day compute budget, models of different size reach similar final MLM loss (~1.9). Larger models learn faster per token, but smaller models process more tokens.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Near a fixed compute budget, final loss is insensitive to model size over a wide range, because per-token efficiency trades off against throughput.

record.problems: The loss is reported as MLM loss, with held-out status not stated. Figure 1 provides no fitted exponents or numerical loss points in the text. Tables 8 and 9 do not state parameter counts for individual architecture variants, limiting conclusions about shape at fixed parameter count.
record.rows_left_out: None. Rows r2–r35 record the architecture results in Table 8; rows r36–r60 record the architecture results in Table 9.

untested.parts: No power-law fit, exponents or numeric loss-vs-N/D/C points. The 'scaling laws hold' statement is qualitative (Figure 1 only).
No fixed-compute allocation sweep with fitted exponents.
Depth and width variants in Tables 8 and 9 are compared at fixed wall-clock time, not fixed parameter count, and parameter counts are not given.
GLUE is reported but not related to scale or loss.

missing.what: Ablation block of the final architecture: decoder bias 1.84, eps 1.83, learned emb 1.83, no norm after emb 1.89, no final norm 1.85, no skip 1.83, QKV bias 1.83, linear bias 1.84, 4 heads 1.88, rotary 1.86, Post-LN 7.54, Fourier 2.65, GELU 1.83. rows_left_out wrongly says none were omitted.

record.verdict_notes: Figure 1 has no numeric values in the text, so r1 rests on the authors' words. Table 8 and Table 9 depth/width rows vary the parameter count at fixed time, so they cannot isolate V4. They are left as cannot_determine.

versions.untested_parts: The study reports MLM loss, but does not state that it is held-out loss or fit and report power-law exponents. It does not isolate parameter count, tokens, and compute in the manner of the original scaling-law measurement.
No small-run fit is used to predict the loss of substantially larger runs.
No sweep finds the loss-minimising parameter/token allocation at fixed compute or fits its trend.

The text says architecture type has little effect after accounting for model size, but the tables do not state parameter counts for each variant, so they do not independently establish fixed-parameter comparisons.
The study is text MLM pretraining. It does not test other modalities or training regimes for the same power-law form.
Downstream GLUE performance is reported, but its predictability from scale or pretraining loss is not tested.
The study does not test how fitted exponents or compute-optimal allocations vary with fitting choices, nor whether fitted loss curves bend away from a power law.

rows.value: The text says trajectories are unpredictable during the first 1B tokens; thereafter per-token efficiencies differ by a multiplicative constant that depends almost entirely on model size, not model type. All choices reach an MLM loss around 1.9 at the end.
rows.locator: Figure 1 and Section 4.2, “Scaling laws hold in the low-resource regime”
rows.note: This is an aggregate textual report of the figure, not a held-out-loss measurement or an explicit power-law fit. The authors characterize these results as evidence that scaling laws hold in this low-resource setting.
rows.check: Bears on V4: per-token loss after the first 1B tokens depends on model size, not type. It cannot show V1, because there is no power-law fit or numeric curve and the loss is not stated to be held-out. For V1 it would be cannot_determine.

relationships.condition: Transformer variants after the first 1B tokens; fixed-parameter detail changes (heads, biases, norms, embeddings)
relationships.reason: Per-token loss depends on size, not type (r1). Head-count, bias, norm and embedding changes at near-fixed params move loss by at most 0.05 (r25-r31, r33-r35).
relationships.display_finding: Changing attention heads, biases, normalization or embeddings at nearly fixed parameters moved loss by at most 0.05.

relationships.condition: Post-LN placement under the aggressive one-cycle LR recipe
relationships.reason: Post-LN at near-fixed params gives MLM loss 7.54 vs 1.89, i.e. training fails. Authors tie pre-norm to enabling the large LR (r32).
relationships.display_finding: Post-LN produced MLM loss 7.54 versus 1.89 at nearly equal parameters, with pre-norm enabling the large learning rate.
